genesFromGenerange.note: The one engine input this scenario has that the state trace cannot supply: a gene-bound property needs a gene source (`ctx.engine.genes`), or `run_cppprops.mjs` exits 1 with 'gene binding: no gene source'. The table is parsed out of the recorded run's own `run/genome/meta/generange.txt` (kept verbatim as `native/gene_dyn.generange.txt`): `MateEnergyFraction` is `None FLOAT 0.500000 FLOAT 0.800000 MateEnergyFraction`, i.e. `{kind: FLOAT, min: 0.5, max: 0.8}` - the gene range the worldfile's `dyn( 0.5 )` sets, which is also what the port's genome layer reproduces (tests/cppprops-gene-binding.test.ts pins `geneTableFromGenomeUtil` against this very line). Nothing is typed here: `names` only says which gene the spec's `$[gene, MateEnergyFraction, min]` symbol reads.

Alive0 == AgentCount at every recorded step (single-metabolism scenario: the worldfile is growers_dyn with one added dyn form, and the recorded ordering difference between AgentCount and AgentMetabolisms[0] is handled by the mapping, not by the values).
gene_dyn.crosscheckNote: Byte-identical to `native/gene_dyn.generated.cc`, including the schema location in the emitted error text: line 153 is `genome::GenomeUtil::getGene( "MateEnergyFraction", "./etc/worldfile.wfs:1619: Cannot find gene 'MateEnergyFraction'" )`, whose `path:line` is native `propSym.getLocation().getDescription()` - the *schema* document's own name (`./etc/worldfile.wfs`, the literal native Simulation.cc:270 passes to buildSchemaDocument) and the line of the schema's `cppsym` property. `verify_cppprops.py` derives that name from this manifest's `native_root` + `schema` and hands it to the extractor as `--schema-name`; a wrong derivation fails the crosscheck instead of passing with a plausible path. No exemption is needed (it was ported rather than waived).
gene_dyn.propertyNote: growers_dyn.wf with one added form on `MinEnergyFractionToOffspring` (whose schema cppsym is the gene read `$[gene, MateEnergyFraction, min]`): `dyn( 0.5 ) { if( Step < 10 ) return value; return min( 0.5, value + 0.001 ); }`. The gene's minimum is what the property *is* (its storage is `...->smin.__val`), and `MinEnergyFractionToOffspring` configures `MateEnergyFraction.min`, so the gene value and the worldfile value coincide - the recorded `generange.txt` says `FLOAT 0.500000` where the same worldfile without the dyn form says `0.200000`. The farm log carries the property as the added `term.mf` entry `MinEFOff`, 0.5 on all 300 steps (1 distinct value); the discriminating evidence for the *binding* is synthetic (a spec seeded 0.9 that must serve 0.2), see tests/cppprops-gene-binding.test.ts. `term.mf`'s added entry is additive: FarmMonitor skips a monitored name that is not in the metadata table, so no other scenario's log changes.

growers_ring.stateKeyNote: runtime property -> key in state/<scn>.state.json; the trace comes from Simulation::getStatusText (independent of the cppprops path). This scenario also records the per-patch `foodPatches` block (`Simulation.cc` getStatusText FP lines): steps[i]["foodPatches"]["<domain>.<patch>"]["agentInsideCount"].
growers_ring.engineNote: engineFromState feeds the FoodPatchTokenRing binding its `FoodPatch::agentInsideCount` input per step (verify_cppprops.py -> run_cppprops.mjs --engine). `table` names the engine table, `field` the state key it is read from, and `stepShift` which state record step N's table comes from (N + stepShift): -1, because the counts are accumulated at the END of a step (DeathAndStats, reached from Interact, after the agents have moved) while the ring runs at the START of it (CppProperties::update at Simulation.cc:648) - so the ring at step N reads the counts printed for step N-1, and step 1 reads the initial zeros. Measured against the native farm log, not fitted: shift -1 reproduces all 300 steps; shift 0 diverges at step 26 and shift +1 at step 25 (Domains[0].FoodPatches[1].On: interpreter False, native True) - those are the crossings where FP1's agentInsideCount reaches maxPopulation 2 only after the step-7 kill emptied the patch. See docs/specs/cppprops.md 8.2.
growers_ring.propertyNote: growers_small/growers_dyn's worldfile with the FIRST token ring's parameter set lowered so the ring actually switches inside the 300-step window: `FoodPatchTokenRing::add( FoodPatches[0], 150, 2000, 400 )` -> `( 2, 20, 5 )`. 2 rather than the step-1 counts themselves (23/24/40), because a threshold inside the range the counts already sit in fires at step 2 under any alignment; 2 is reached again only by counting agents into a patch a previous cycle emptied, and those crossings are what pin the step alignment (see engineNote). Everything else is byte-identical to growers_dyn.wf (which never switches patch: P0On=True, P1On=P2On=False for all 300 steps). Measured in the native farm log: 35 P*On transitions covering all three ring branches - the maxPopulation branch with its delay window (12 transitions into 000, e.g. step 2 and step 28), the delayEnd findActive() / "kill agents in the new patch" path (12 transitions 000 -> *, e.g. step 7: the alive count drops 181 -> 139, and the run's own `-patch` death counter is non-zero), and the timeout/findImmediate branch (11 transitions * -> * with no delay window, e.g. step 27 and step 53).

two_metabolisms.stateKeyNote: runtime property -> key in state/<scn>.state.json; the state trace comes from Simulation::getStatusText (independent of the cppprops path). This scenario defines TWO metabolisms, so getStatusText prints ` -<Name> = <n>` per definition (Simulation.cc:4894-4904) and the state trace records them directly: `metabolism<j>` is `fNumberAliveWithMetabolism[ Metabolism::get( j )->index ]`, i.e. the value the `AgentMetabolisms[j].MetabolismAgentCount` cppsym reads -- a recording, not an inference from `agents`. The recorded order is the definition order; the names it printed are `metabolismNames` in the state file, and `-Alpha = 12 -Beta = 13` at step 1 (vs `agents = 25`) is what pins AgentMetabolisms[0] to Alpha -- the farm log's independent Alive0=12 agrees.
two_metabolisms.propertyNote: minitest.wf + an explicit `AgentMetabolisms [ { Name "Alpha" } { Name "Beta" } ]` and `AgentMetabolismSelectionMode Random`; nothing else differs (first 17 lines byte-identical). Two definitions is the gate that makes getStatusText print the per-metabolism counts; Random spreads agents (and newborns) over both (agent.cc:490-505), so the counts split 12/13 at step 1 and diverge from `agents` at every one of the 301 steps (min 11, max 15, median 13); `metabolism0 + metabolism1 == agents` holds at all 301 steps (the counts partition the alive agents, deaths/births included). The farm log samples the four properties term.mf lists, so Alive0 is the native value of AgentMetabolisms[0].MetabolismAgentCount and no longer equals AgentCount.
